title: A fixed-map orbit cone converts integrated squared disturbance into a cubic pointwise bound

statement.quantifiers: One finite stationary CPTP Phi, ONE fixed CPTP Psi satisfying e_Psi(x)^2<=a J_forward(x) on all orbit states, and faithful rho/reference weight.
statement.assertion: e_Psi(rho)^3<=6a D(rho||omega) T(rho,id tensor Phi(rho)); singular closure if both maps fix omega.
assumptions: Physical entropy differentiation along original Poisson orbit and genuine Umegaki D.
Same comparator at every state/time; half trace distance.

inputs: All-state fixed-map error-energy bound, stationary weight and original channel residual.
outputs: Cubic disturbance with exact cone factor six.
interface.precision: Finite-time integration then monotone limit; no spectral gap or unique limiting state needed.
costs: No free conversion from observational radius to genuine relative entropy.
Common map acquisition and atom/precision costs remain separate.

proof_mechanism: Original orbit contraction gives T(rho_t,rho)<=t b.
Fixed CPTP Psi error is 2-Lipschitz, so e_t>=(e-2tb)_+.
Exact integral of squared cone is e^3/(6b); handle b=0 without division.
Dilute with fixed omega; both residuals scale, D continuous.
obstructions: Per-state comparator selection cannot be integrated as one error function.
Reference/local marginal D term cannot be dropped without exact margin equality.

potential_uses.transfer_gate: Prove an all-state bound, orbit speed and fixed-map Lipschitz constant before deriving a pointwise power law.

review.source_reported: Source reports internally reconstructed and adversarially audited mathematics with scoped finite checks; no independent ingestion proof reconstruction, scientific replay, external correctness or priority clearance.
